title: Knowledge check: Encapsulating jQuery Behavior

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of encapsulating jquery behavior?
options: Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers.
questions.explanation: Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying immediately invoked function expressions (iifes)?
options: Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use immediately invoked function expressions (iifes) deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use immediately invoked function expressions (iifes) deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with encapsulating jquery behavior?
options: Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
